content.overview: BNS s. 136 — Assault or criminal force on grave provocation.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Assault or criminal force on grave provocation. BNS restatement of IPC 358. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 358. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 136 is the rule on “Assault or criminal force on grave provocation”. The section provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 136 exists so that “Assault or criminal force on grave provocation” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
